issues_outside_coverage: Whether Missouri state law termination-at-death rule satisfies sec. 71(b)(1)(D) (addressed in dicta; requires a finding of statutory maintenance obligation)
decisive_judgment_findings: The agreement, amended agreement, and judgment each state that neither party shall pay or receive maintenance, which the court treated as a clear, explicit and express designation that the payments are not alimony (sec. 71(b)(1)(B)).
No Missouri court found Ms. Edington eligible for maintenance; she was continuously employed, bought a home, and could support herself, so the payments were not shown to be statutory maintenance.
Supervisor approved the penalty in writing on May 8, 2019, before the first formal communication (30-day letter of May 10, 2019).
Petitioner claimed the deduction despite instruments explicitly denying maintenance; no reasonable cause or good faith shown; no authorities identified.
